name: LF framing preserves Unicode string data in tracker exports
summary: Tracker exports and native JSONL results use LF as the physical row delimiter. Unicode NEL, line separator and paragraph separator inside valid JSON strings remain part of the same row; decoded titles, descriptions, comments and labels keep their text. CRLF remains accepted as JSON whitespace at the physical boundary. Shared row readers retain their existing nesting limits and malformed-row markers. Independent export readers and the credential name rule retain their existing refusal behavior for actually unreadable, cut or non-row output; an unreadable row never frees a held name. This proposal is a delivery payload for review, not an accepted or activated index entry.
